words.enDefinition: conventions for behaving considerately in interactions with other people

examples.en: Our orientation included a short discussion about social etiquette in shared study spaces.
examples.zh: 迎新活动简短讨论了共享自习空间里的「社交礼仪」。

examples.en: The club's social etiquette handout suggested asking before sharing photos of other members.
examples.zh: 社团的「社交礼仪」资料建议，分享其他成员的照片前先问一声。

collocations: learn about social etiquette
discuss social etiquette
social etiquette in a shared space

words.enDefinition: ordinary consideration people show each other in everyday situations

examples.en: My roommate picked up the dropped scarf as a matter of common courtesy.
examples.zh: 室友顺手捡起掉在地上的围巾，觉得这是「基本礼貌」。

examples.en: The notice described returning the chairs after the session as a common courtesy.
examples.zh: 通知说，活动结束后把椅子归位，是一种「基本礼貌」。

collocations: show common courtesy
a matter of common courtesy
an act of common courtesy

words.enDefinition: a convention people generally follow without seeing it formally stated

examples.en: One unwritten rule in our study group was to let the speaker finish.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组有条「不成文的规矩」，就是让发言的人把话说完。

examples.en: Our club had an unwritten rule about leaving the front row for guests.
examples.zh: 我们社团有条「不成文的规矩」，把第一排留给来宾。

collocations: follow an unwritten rule
learn an unwritten rule
an unwritten rule in a group

words.enDefinition: to take another person's example as a guide for your actions

examples.en: It's fine to follow someone's lead when you're unsure which seats are reserved.
examples.zh: 拿不准哪些座位被预留了，可以先「照着别人的做法来」。

examples.en: I thought I'd follow someone's lead instead of guessing where to put my coat.
examples.zh: 我想「照着别人的做法来」，不自己猜外套该放哪儿。

collocations: decide to follow someone's lead
be ready to follow someone's lead
quietly follow someone's lead

words.enDefinition: to notice how others feel and adapt your behaviour accordingly

examples.en: I tried to read the room before making a joke during the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论时，我先「察看现场气氛」，再决定要不要开玩笑。

examples.en: My teammate stopped halfway through the story and took a moment to read the room.
examples.zh: 队友讲到一半停了停，「察看现场气氛」。

collocations: try to read the room
learn to read the room
pause to read the room

words.enDefinition: a title used with a name to show respect

examples.en: The form let each speaker choose an honorific for the printed programme.
examples.zh: 表格让每位发言者为印制的活动手册挑选一个「姓名前的敬称」。

examples.en: I checked which honorific the guest used before writing the name on the card.
examples.zh: 在卡片上写名字前，我查了来宾使用哪个「敬称」。

collocations: choose an honorific
use an honorific before a name
omit the honorific

words.enDefinition: a respectful way of referring to someone using both elements

examples.en: I used her title and surname when addressing her in the public session.
examples.zh: 我在公开活动上称呼她时用了「头衔加姓氏」。

examples.en: The organiser printed each guest's title and surname on the reserved seat card.
examples.zh: 组织者在预留座位的卡片上印了每位来宾的「头衔加姓氏」。

collocations: use a title and surname
a guest's title and surname
address someone by their title and surname

words.enDefinition: the name or title someone wants others to use

examples.en: The organiser asked each guest about their preferred form of address before the panel.
examples.zh: 座谈开始前，组织者向每位来宾问了他们「希望别人怎么称呼自己」。

examples.en: I wrote the tutor's preferred form of address on a note by my screen.
examples.zh: 我在屏幕旁的便签上记下了导师「希望使用的称呼」。

collocations: ask about someone's preferred form of address
note the preferred form of address
use someone's preferred form of address

words.enDefinition: to leave out the title when using someone's name

examples.en: My tutor said I could skip the title when writing to her directly.
examples.zh: 导师说，直接给她写信时「不用加头衔」。

examples.en: The guest asked me to skip the title on their informal name badge.
examples.zh: 来宾请我在非正式活动的胸牌上「不用加头衔」。

collocations: ask someone to skip the title
feel free to skip the title
agree to skip the title

words.enDefinition: a title placed before a man's surname or full name

examples.en: The moderator introduced him as Mr Patel before handing him the microphone.
examples.zh: 主持人把麦克风递给他之前，介绍他是 Patel「先生」。

examples.en: The host wrote Mr Green on the name card beside the lectern.
examples.zh: 主持人在讲台旁的姓名卡上写了 Green「先生」。

collocations: Mr before a surname
address someone as Mr Patel
use the title Mr

words.enDefinition: a title traditionally used before the surname of a married woman

examples.en: The guest asked us to call her Mrs Lewis during the awards ceremony.
examples.zh: 来宾请我们在颁奖典礼上称她为 Lewis「太太」。

examples.en: The speech notes used Mrs Shah, the title she had entered on the form.
examples.zh: 发言稿用了 Shah「太太」，这是她自己在表格上填的称谓。

collocations: Mrs before a surname
address someone as Mrs Lewis
use the title Mrs

words.enDefinition: a title used before a name without indicating gender

examples.en: The speaker had selected Mx on the form, so I used it on their badge.
examples.zh: 发言者在表格上选了「无性别敬称 Mx」，我便把它写在了对方的胸牌上。

examples.en: The staff list gave the volunteer's name as Mx Lane for the welcome session.
examples.zh: 迎新活动的工作人员名单把那位志愿者写作「Mx Lane」。

collocations: use the title Mx
place Mx before a surname
address someone as Mx Lane

words.enDefinition: a title used in academic contexts before a doctorate holder's name

examples.en: The coordinator introduced Dr Chen before she began speaking about the community project.
examples.zh: 协调员介绍了陈「博士」，随后她开始谈那个社区项目。

examples.en: I used Dr Malik on the programme because that was their request.
examples.zh: 我按对方的要求，在活动手册上写了马利克「博士」。

collocations: Dr before a surname
address someone as Dr Chen
use the title Dr

words.enDefinition: a formal title that refers to someone's academic role or qualification

examples.en: I checked the academic title on the biography before introducing our guest speaker.
examples.zh: 介绍来宾发言人前，我查看了简介上的「学术头衔」。

examples.en: The invitation listed the speaker's academic title beneath her name and photo.
examples.zh: 邀请函在发言者的姓名和照片下方列了她的「学术头衔」。

collocations: check someone's academic title
use the correct academic title
include an academic title

words.enDefinition: a written or recorded aid for saying a name correctly

examples.en: The event organiser sent a name pronunciation guide before our practice introductions.
examples.zh: 我们练习介绍来宾前，活动组织者发来了一份「姓名读音指南」。

examples.en: I listened to the name pronunciation guide while walking to the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我走去讲堂时听了「姓名读音指南」的录音。

collocations: provide a name pronunciation guide
use a name pronunciation guide
an audio name pronunciation guide

words.enDefinition: to say a person's name with the wrong sounds or stress

examples.en: I didn't want to mispronounce a name during the club's award ceremony.
examples.zh: 我不想在社团颁奖典礼上「读错姓名」。

examples.en: It's easy to mispronounce a name if you've only seen it written down.
examples.zh: 如果只见过书写形式，就容易「读错姓名」。

collocations: accidentally mispronounce a name
try not to mispronounce a name
worry you'll mispronounce a name

words.enDefinition: with a family name written or spoken before given names

examples.en: The attendance sheet listed her surname first, but the name badge didn't.
examples.zh: 签到表上她的「姓氏在前」，胸牌上却不是。

examples.en: I kept the surname first because that was the order he'd given me.
examples.zh: 我保留了「姓氏在前」的顺序，因为这是他交给我的写法。

collocations: write the surname first
list the surname first
put the surname first

words.enDefinition: to write the letters of a person's name in the correct order

examples.en: I checked the list to spell a name correctly on the group card.
examples.zh: 我核对了名单，好在联名卡片上「把姓名拼对」。

examples.en: The coordinator reminded us to spell a name correctly on every certificate we printed.
examples.zh: 协调员提醒我们，打印证书时都要「把姓名拼对」。

collocations: check that you spell a name correctly
learn to spell a name correctly
make sure you spell a name correctly

words.enDefinition: to get to a place shortly before the planned time

examples.en: I tried to arrive a few minutes early so I could find a seat.
examples.zh: 我尽量「提前几分钟到场」，好先找个座位。

examples.en: The organiser asked us to arrive a few minutes early for the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 组织者请我们「提前几分钟到场」参加排练。

collocations: plan to arrive a few minutes early
be asked to arrive a few minutes early
arrive a few minutes early to settle in

words.enDefinition: to reach a place before it is convenient for you to be there

examples.en: I didn't want to arrive too early while the volunteers were setting up.
examples.zh: 志愿者还在布置现场，我不想「到得太早」。

examples.en: We agreed not to arrive too early because the hall doors were still locked.
examples.zh: 礼堂门还锁着，我们商量好别「到得太早」。

collocations: try not to arrive too early
worry you'll arrive too early
arrive too early for a meeting

words.enDefinition: to make another person wait longer than expected

examples.en: I didn't want to keep someone waiting while I looked for my coat.
examples.zh: 我找外套时不想「让别人一直等」。

examples.en: Our coordinator said it was easy to keep someone waiting when a message went unread.
examples.zh: 协调员说，消息要是一直没被看到，就容易「让别人一直等」。

collocations: try not to keep someone waiting
feel bad about keeping someone waiting
keep someone waiting on purpose

words.expression: let them know you'll be late
words.lemma: let them know you'll be late
words.zhGloss: 提前告诉对方你会迟到
words.enDefinition: to tell the people expecting you that you will arrive late
acceptedZhAnswers: 提前告诉对方你会迟到
acceptedEnVariants: let them know you'll be late

examples.en: “Let them know you'll be late,” my tutor said when class ran over.
examples.zh: 课程拖堂时，导师说「要提前告诉对方你会迟到」。

examples.en: My roommate said, “Let them know you'll be late,” when the bus stopped.
examples.zh: 公交车停下时，室友说「要提前告诉对方你会迟到」。

collocations: remember to let them know you'll be late
let them know you'll be late by text
let them know you'll be late before the start

words.enDefinition: the time everyone has agreed an activity will begin

examples.en: I arrived before the agreed start time so we could begin together.
examples.zh: 我在「约好的开始时间」之前到了，这样大家可以一起开始。

examples.en: We moved the agreed start time after checking with everyone in the group.
examples.zh: 确认过所有小组成员的情况后，我们改了「约好的开始时间」。

collocations: confirm the agreed start time
a change to the agreed start time
be there by the agreed start time

words.enDefinition: to reach a place at or before the stated time

examples.en: Our invitation asked us to arrive by six for the student awards evening.
examples.zh: 学生颁奖晚会的邀请函请我们「最迟六点到」。

examples.en: The coordinator said I should arrive by noon to help with seating.
examples.zh: 协调员说，我应该「最迟中午到」，帮忙安排座位。

collocations: arrive by the stated time
arrive by six
ask guests to arrive by noon

words.enDefinition: to go away during a pause rather than while an event continues

examples.en: I asked if I could leave during the break to catch the bus.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「在中场休息时离开」，好去赶公交。

examples.en: We decided to leave during the break so we wouldn't interrupt the lecture.
examples.zh: 我们决定「在中场休息时离开」，这样不会打断讲座。

collocations: plan to leave during the break
ask whether you can leave during the break
quietly leave during the break

words.enDefinition: to avoid making other people wait or spend time unnecessarily

examples.en: Our committee tried to respect people's time by ending each meeting as planned.
examples.zh: 委员会尽量「尊重别人的时间」，每次会议都按计划结束。

examples.en: She explained that sticking to our schedule was a way to respect people's time.
examples.zh: 她解释说，按时间表行事是「尊重别人的时间」的一种方式。

collocations: try to respect people's time
show that you respect people's time
respect people's time by starting promptly

words.enDefinition: a person who arrives after an activity has already started

examples.en: The usher quietly showed a latecomer to a seat near the door.
examples.zh: 引座员轻声指给一名「迟到的人」门边的座位。

examples.en: The only latecomer at the talk waited until the applause to enter.
examples.zh: 讲座唯一「迟到的人」等到掌声响起才走进来。

collocations: show a latecomer to a seat
admit latecomers during a break
seats reserved for latecomers

words.enDefinition: to come after an activity has already begun

examples.en: The theatre asked anyone who might arrive after the start to wait outside.
examples.zh: 剧场请可能「在活动开始后到场」的人先在外面等。

examples.en: I knew I'd arrive after the start, so I checked the late entry policy.
examples.zh: 我知道会「在活动开始后到场」，便先查了迟到入场规定。

collocations: expect to arrive after the start
be likely to arrive after the start
guests who arrive after the start

words.enDefinition: a venue's rules for admitting people after an event has begun

examples.en: I checked the late entry policy because my evening class might run over.
examples.zh: 晚课可能拖堂，我就查了「迟到入场规定」。

examples.en: The late entry policy was printed on the back of the concert ticket.
examples.zh: 音乐会门票的背面印着「迟到入场规定」。

collocations: check the late entry policy
publish a late entry policy
follow the venue's late entry policy

words.enDefinition: the area around someone that they expect people to respect

examples.en: I moved my chair back to give my classmate more personal space.
examples.zh: 我把椅子往后挪了挪，给同学多留一些「个人空间」。

examples.en: My friend said she needed personal space when the room became crowded.
examples.zh: 房间里人一多，朋友就说她需要一点「个人空间」。

collocations: give someone personal space
respect personal space
invade someone's personal space

words.enDefinition: to stand nearer to someone than they are comfortable with

examples.en: I tried not to stand too close while we waited for the lift.
examples.zh: 我们等电梯时，我尽量别「站得太近」。

examples.en: It's easy to stand too close when you cannot hear the person speaking.
examples.zh: 听不清对方讲话时，很容易「站得太近」。

collocations: try not to stand too close
stand too close to someone
feel someone stand too close

words.enDefinition: at a distance approximately equal to the length of an arm

examples.en: We stood an arm's length away from each other during the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练时，我们彼此「相隔一臂远」。

examples.en: The photographer asked me to stand an arm's length away from the chair.
examples.zh: 摄影师让我站到和椅子「相隔一臂远」的地方。

collocations: stand an arm's length away
sit an arm's length away
stay about an arm's length away

words.enDefinition: a conversation held quietly enough not to disturb other people

examples.en: We had a hushed conversation in the corridor while the speaker answered questions.
examples.zh: 发言者回答提问时，我们在走廊里「低声交谈」。

examples.en: I heard a hushed conversation behind me while the library film was playing.
examples.zh: 图书馆放电影时，我听见身后有人「低声交谈」。

collocations: have a hushed conversation
hear a hushed conversation
a hushed conversation in the corridor

words.enDefinition: to speak at a quieter level appropriate for an indoor space

examples.en: My friend smiled and asked me to use an indoor voice in the café.
examples.zh: 朋友笑着请我在咖啡馆「在室内小声说话」。

examples.en: The volunteer reminded the visiting children to use an indoor voice near the library.
examples.zh: 志愿者提醒来参观的孩子在图书馆附近「小声说话」。

collocations: please use an indoor voice
remember to use an indoor voice
ask someone to use an indoor voice

words.enDefinition: to step outside to handle a phone call without disturbing others

examples.en: I offered to take the call outside when my phone started buzzing.
examples.zh: 手机开始振动时，我说可以「出去接电话」。

examples.en: My classmate chose to take the call outside before our study session began.
examples.zh: 自习开始前，同学决定「出去接电话」。

collocations: decide to take the call outside
ask someone to take the call outside
step out to take the call outside

words.enDefinition: to let audio play through a speaker where others can hear it

examples.en: I asked my friend not to play it out loud on the bus.
examples.zh: 我请朋友在公交车上别「把声音外放」。

examples.en: She asked before deciding to play it out loud in the common room.
examples.zh: 她先问了一声，再决定要不要在公共休息室「把声音外放」。

collocations: don't play it out loud
choose to play it out loud
ask before you play it out loud

words.enDefinition: to listen through headphones to avoid playing sound into a shared space

examples.en: I chose to use headphones so my music wouldn't bother the people studying.
examples.zh: 我选择「戴耳机听」，免得音乐打扰正在自习的人。

examples.en: The train announcement asked passengers to use headphones for their own videos.
examples.zh: 车上广播请乘客看自己的视频时「戴耳机听」。

collocations: use headphones on public transport
ask people to use headphones
use headphones for audio

words.enDefinition: to make your phone vibrate rather than ring for notifications

examples.en: The host said, “Set your phone to vibrate if you need it on.”
examples.zh: 主持人说，如果手机要开着，就「把它设成振动」。

examples.en: The notice said to set your phone to vibrate before entering the studio.
examples.zh: 通知说，进工作室之前先「把手机设成振动」。

collocations: please set your phone to vibrate
remember to set your phone to vibrate
set your phone to vibrate during the event

words.enDefinition: an area where people are asked not to use phones

examples.en: The entrance sign described the small gallery as a phone-free zone during performances.
examples.zh: 入口标牌上说，演出期间，小展厅是「禁用手机的区域」。

examples.en: Our club made the rehearsal room a phone-free zone for one evening.
examples.zh: 社团把排练室设成了一晚上的「禁用手机的区域」。

collocations: designate a phone-free zone
enter a phone-free zone
a sign for a phone-free zone

words.enDefinition: a notice asking people not to make an audio or video recording

examples.en: The sign said “No recording” above the door of the student screening room.
examples.zh: 学生放映室的门上方写着「禁止录音录像」。

examples.en: I saw “No recording” on the first slide of the club's rehearsal.
examples.zh: 社团排练的第一张幻灯片上写着「禁止录音录像」。

collocations: a “No recording” sign
display “No recording”
a room marked “No recording”

words.enDefinition: to ask another person whether they want to sit where you are sitting

examples.en: Our tutor said you can offer someone your seat with a simple question.
examples.zh: 导师说，想「给别人让座」，简单问一声就行。

examples.en: It can feel awkward to offer someone your seat in a crowded room.
examples.zh: 房间里很挤时，主动「给别人让座」可能会觉得有点尴尬。

collocations: choose to offer someone your seat
offer someone your seat on the bus
politely offer someone your seat

words.enDefinition: to wait for people to leave before you enter

examples.en: I stepped back to let people out first when the lift doors opened.
examples.zh: 电梯门一开，我往后退了退，「先让里面的人出来」。

examples.en: The attendant asked us to let people out first at the hall entrance.
examples.zh: 引座员让我们在礼堂门口「先让里面的人出来」。

collocations: wait and let people out first
let people out first before entering
remember to let people out first

words.expression: is this the end of the line
words.lemma: is this the end of the line
words.enDefinition: a question checking where people should join a queue
acceptedEnVariants: is this the end of the line

examples.en: The queue curved around the corner, so I asked, “Is this the end of the line?”
examples.zh: 队伍拐过了街角，我就问「这里是队尾吗？」

examples.en: “Is this the end of the line?” my friend asked outside the hall.
examples.zh: 朋友在礼堂外问「这里是队尾吗？」

collocations: ask “Is this the end of the line?”
“Excuse me, is this the end of the line?”
“Is this the end of the line for the talk?”

words.enDefinition: a queue rule against keeping a place for someone who is absent

examples.en: A sign said “No place saving” by the queue for student tickets.
examples.zh: 学生票队伍旁的标牌写着「请勿替人占排队位置」。

examples.en: The organiser repeated “No place saving” when the line began to fill.
examples.zh: 队伍开始变长时，组织者又提醒了一次「请勿替人占排队位置」。

collocations: a “No place saving” rule
a sign saying “No place saving”
announce “No place saving”

words.enDefinition: to stand one person behind another in one line

examples.en: We were asked to stand in single file near the coat check.
examples.zh: 工作人员请我们在衣帽间旁「排成一列站好」。

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to the marker and asked us to stand in single file.
examples.zh: 志愿者指着标记，请我们「排成一列站好」。

collocations: ask people to stand in single file
stand in single file near the entrance
remember to stand in single file

words.expression: let someone go ahead of you
words.lemma: let someone go ahead of you
words.enDefinition: to allow another person to take a turn before you
acceptedEnVariants: let someone go ahead of you

examples.en: You could let someone go ahead of you while you looked for your ticket.
examples.zh: 找票时，你可以「让别人排到你前面」。

examples.en: My friend asked if you could let someone go ahead of you in line here.
examples.zh: 朋友问在这里排队能不能「让别人排到你前面」。

collocations: choose to let someone go ahead of you
let someone go ahead of you in line
offer to let someone go ahead of you

words.enDefinition: to make space for a neighbour to use the same armrest

examples.en: We managed to share the armrest once we had settled into our seats.
examples.zh: 我们坐定后，顺利地「共用了座椅扶手」。

examples.en: I tried to share the armrest without nudging the person beside me.
examples.zh: 我想不碰到旁边的人，跟对方「共用那个座椅扶手」。

collocations: agree to share the armrest
try to share the armrest
share the armrest with the person next to you

words.enDefinition: to keep a seat free until another person arrives

examples.en: I asked whether I could save a seat for someone during the talk.
examples.zh: 我问讲座期间能不能「替别人留座」。

examples.en: The usher said we could save a seat for someone until the play started.
examples.zh: 引座员说，开演前我们可以「替别人留座」。

collocations: offer to save a seat for someone
ask if you can save a seat for someone
save a seat for someone near the aisle

words.zhGloss: 结束之前请留在座位上
words.enDefinition: to stay in your seat until a performance or activity is over
acceptedZhAnswers: 结束之前请留在座位上

examples.en: The programme asked the audience to remain seated until the end of the performance.
examples.zh: 活动手册请观众「在演出结束之前留在座位上」。

examples.en: I decided to remain seated until the end so I wouldn't block anyone's view.
examples.zh: 我决定「结束之前留在座位上」，免得挡住别人。

collocations: ask people to remain seated until the end
choose to remain seated until the end
please remain seated until the end

words.enDefinition: to keep from standing where others cannot see past you

examples.zh: 我决定大家吃饭时不「提起敏感话题」。

examples.en: Our facilitator asked us to check before we bring up a sensitive topic.
examples.zh: 引导员请我们在「提起敏感话题」前先问问大家。

collocations: avoid bringing up a sensitive topic
choose when to bring up a sensitive topic
ask before you bring up a sensitive topic

words.enDefinition: to say something about a person's appearance, habits or character

examples.en: I try not to make a personal remark when commenting on someone's work.
examples.zh: 我对别人的作品发表意见时，尽量不「对别人作私人评价」。

examples.en: The moderator asked us not to make a personal remark about any speaker.
examples.zh: 主持人请我们不要「对发言者作私人评价」。

collocations: try not to make a personal remark
make a personal remark about someone's appearance
be tempted to make a personal remark

words.enDefinition: to express an opinion about how another person looks

examples.en: I felt it wasn't the right moment to comment on someone's appearance.
examples.zh: 我觉得那时候不适合「评论别人的外表」。

examples.en: The workshop discussed when it might be unwelcome to comment on someone's appearance.
examples.zh: 工作坊讨论了哪些情况下「评论别人的外表」可能让人不舒服。

collocations: choose whether to comment on someone's appearance
hesitate to comment on someone's appearance
try not to comment on someone's appearance

words.expression: make a joke at someone's expense
words.lemma: make a joke at someone's expense
words.enDefinition: to make a joke that makes someone else look foolish
acceptedEnVariants: make a joke at someone's expense

examples.en: I didn't want to make a joke at someone's expense during the introductions.
examples.zh: 我不想在介绍环节「拿别人开玩笑」。

examples.en: The club's moderator asked us not to make a joke at someone's expense.
examples.zh: 社团主持人请我们不要「拿别人开玩笑」。

collocations: try not to make a joke at someone's expense
choose not to make a joke at someone's expense
be careful not to make a joke at someone's expense

words.enDefinition: a joke considered indecent or unsuitable for the occasion

examples.en: An off-color joke made the conversation stop for a moment at our table.
examples.zh: 有人讲了个「粗俗的笑话」，我们那桌一时没人说话。

examples.en: The host changed the subject after hearing an off-color joke from the audience.
examples.zh: 听到观众讲了个「粗俗的笑话」后，主持人换了话题。

collocations: tell an off-color joke
hear an off-color joke
react to an off-color joke

words.enDefinition: likely to offend or upset people because it shows poor judgment

examples.en: I thought the comment was in poor taste after our friend had left.
examples.zh: 朋友走后，我觉得那条评论「不得体」。

examples.en: The group agreed that the caption was in poor taste for a public poster.
examples.zh: 大家一致觉得，把那句话放在公开海报上「不得体」。

collocations: a remark in poor taste
consider something in poor taste
a joke in poor taste

words.enDefinition: to feel insulted by something another person says or does

examples.en: I could see why someone might take offence at that joke in class.
examples.zh: 我能理解，有人听到课堂上那个玩笑可能会「感觉被冒犯」。

examples.en: My friend didn't take offence when I asked her to repeat my name.
examples.zh: 我请朋友再叫一遍我的名字，她并没有「感觉被冒犯」。

collocations: take offence at a remark
be quick to take offence
take offence at a joke

words.enDefinition: to give an impression of being impolite, whether intended or not

examples.en: I worried that my short reply might come across as rude in writing.
examples.zh: 我担心回复太短，写出来会「让人觉得没礼貌」。

examples.en: She didn't mean to come across as rude when she left the table.
examples.zh: 她离开餐桌时，并不想「让人觉得没礼貌」。

collocations: might come across as rude
worry you'll come across as rude
avoid coming across as rude

words.enDefinition: to go beyond what someone considers socially acceptable

examples.en: The student said a joke can cross a line even among friends.
examples.zh: 那名学生说，朋友之间开的玩笑也可能「超出分寸」。

examples.en: I thought posting the private photo would cross a line in our group.
examples.zh: 我觉得在我们群里发那张私人照会「超出分寸」。

collocations: feel that something would cross a line
cross a line with a joke
be about to cross a line

words.enDefinition: to speak the remaining words before the other person has finished

examples.en: I sometimes rush to finish someone's sentence when I think I know the answer.
examples.zh: 有时我以为知道答案，就「抢着替人把话说完」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us not to finish someone's sentence during the group exercise.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在小组练习时别「抢着替人把话说完」。

collocations: try not to finish someone's sentence
tend to finish someone's sentence
resist the urge to finish someone's sentence

words.enDefinition: to understand a suggestion that was not spoken directly

examples.en: I hoped he would take the hint when I moved back a little.
examples.zh: 我往后挪了挪，希望他能「领会我的暗示」。

examples.en: My friend did not take the hint when I changed the subject twice.
examples.zh: 我两次换话题，朋友还是没「领会我的暗示」。

collocations: fail to take the hint
hope someone will take the hint
quickly take the hint

words.enDefinition: a request to greet without hugging the speaker

examples.en: At the reunion I smiled and said, “No hugs, please,” before waving.
examples.zh: 在重聚会上，我笑着说「请不要拥抱我」，然后挥了挥手。

examples.en: My friend said, “No hugs, please,” and offered a wave instead.
examples.zh: 朋友说「请不要拥抱我」，然后挥手打了个招呼。

collocations: say “No hugs, please”
a badge reading “No hugs, please”
“No hugs, please, but I'd love a wave”

words.expression: wait for someone to offer their hand
words.lemma: wait for someone to offer their hand
words.enDefinition: to let another person choose whether to offer a handshake first
acceptedEnVariants: wait for someone to offer their hand

examples.en: I decided to wait for someone to offer their hand at the reception.
examples.zh: 在招待会上，我决定「等对方先伸手」。

examples.en: Our guide suggested we wait for someone to offer their hand during the introductions.
examples.zh: 向导建议，在介绍环节「等对方先伸手」。

collocations: choose to wait for someone to offer their hand
prefer to wait for someone to offer their hand
wait for someone to offer their hand before shaking

words.enDefinition: conventions for considerate behaviour when communicating online

examples.en: The club discussed netiquette before inviting new members into its online forum.
examples.zh: 社团邀请新成员进线上论坛前，讨论了「网络礼仪」。

examples.en: Our class covered netiquette during the first week of the online project.
examples.zh: 线上项目第一周，我们这门课讲了「网络礼仪」。

collocations: follow basic netiquette
learn about netiquette
a guide to netiquette

words.enDefinition: ways of messaging considerately in a shared chat

examples.en: Our society added a page about group chat etiquette to its welcome notes.
examples.zh: 社团在迎新资料里加了一页「群聊礼仪」。

examples.en: We discussed group chat etiquette after the messages kept arriving through the night.
examples.zh: 晚上消息接连不断，我们便讨论了「群聊礼仪」。

collocations: establish group chat etiquette
discuss group chat etiquette
guidelines on group chat etiquette

words.enDefinition: to get permission before linking another person's account to a post

examples.en: The club asked us to ask before tagging someone in a public photo.
examples.zh: 社团请我们在公开照片里「标注别人前先问一声」。

examples.en: I try to ask before tagging someone in any image from a meeting.
examples.zh: 会议照片里如果要「标注别人，我尽量先问一声」。

collocations: remember to ask before tagging someone
agree to ask before tagging someone
ask before tagging someone in a photo

words.enDefinition: permission to take or use a photograph of a person

examples.en: The committee collected photo consent before taking pictures at the welcome event.
examples.zh: 委员会在迎新活动中拍照前，先征求了「拍照许可」。

examples.en: I checked the photo consent section before sharing the club's group picture.
examples.zh: 分享社团合影前，我查了「照片使用同意」一栏。

collocations: obtain photo consent
a photo consent form
record photo consent

words.expression: keep personal details out of the chat
words.lemma: keep personal details out of the chat
words.zhGloss: 别把私人信息发到群里
words.enDefinition: to avoid putting private information in a shared conversation
acceptedZhAnswers: 别把私人信息发到群里
acceptedEnVariants: keep personal details out of the chat

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to keep personal details out of the chat during the online briefing.
examples.zh: 线上说明会期间，导师请我们「别把私人信息发到群里」。

examples.en: The moderator reminded the group to keep personal details out of the chat.
examples.zh: 群管理员提醒大家「别把私人信息发到群里」。

collocations: ask people to keep personal details out of the chat
remember to keep personal details out of the chat
agree to keep personal details out of the chat

words.enDefinition: to name the creator when passing their work on to others

examples.en: We agreed to give credit when sharing the diagrams made by other students.
examples.zh: 我们约好，分享其他同学做的图示时要「注明出处」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to give credit when sharing anyone else's photos.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在分享别人拍的照片时「注明出处」。

collocations: remember to give credit when sharing
give credit when sharing images
ask members to give credit when sharing

words.enDefinition: to ask whether sharing a message with others is acceptable

examples.en: My friend reminded me to check before forwarding her message to the committee.
examples.zh: 朋友提醒我，把她的消息转给委员会之前「先征求同意」。

examples.en: The class group agreed to check before forwarding photos from the session.
examples.zh: 班级群商定，活动照片「转发前先征求同意」。

collocations: remember to check before forwarding
ask people to check before forwarding
check before forwarding a private message

words.expression: take it to a private chat
words.lemma: take it to a private chat
words.enDefinition: to move a discussion away from a public or group conversation
acceptedEnVariants: take it to a private chat

examples.en: I suggested we take it to a private chat when names came up.
examples.zh: 谈到具体人员的姓名时，我建议「转到私聊去说」。

examples.en: The group moderator asked us to take it to a private chat.
examples.zh: 群管理员请我们「转到私聊去说」。

collocations: suggest taking a topic to a private chat
ask people to take it to a private chat
agree to take it to a private chat

words.zhGloss: 分享号码前先征求同意
words.enDefinition: to get permission before giving someone's phone number to others
acceptedZhAnswers: 分享号码前先征求同意

examples.en: Our group agreed to ask before sharing a number with another club.
examples.zh: 我们小组约定，把成员号码给别的社团前要「先征求同意」。

examples.en: The organiser reminded us to ask before sharing a number from the contact list.
examples.zh: 组织者提醒，分享通讯录里的号码前要「先征求同意」。

collocations: remember to ask before sharing a number
ask everyone to ask before sharing a number
agree to ask before sharing a number

words.enDefinition: a request for permission to be sought before adding you to a group

examples.en: “Don't add me without asking,” my flatmate said after I mentioned the chat.
examples.zh: 我说起那个群聊后，室友说「加我进群前先问一声」。

examples.en: I wrote, “Don't add me without asking,” after leaving the study group chat.
examples.zh: 我退出学习群后写道「加我进群前先问一声」。

collocations: say “Don't add me without asking”
“Don't add me without asking first”
“Please don't add me without asking”

words.enDefinition: a message sent late when the recipient may be resting

examples.en: I saw the late-night message the next morning on my way to class.
examples.zh: 第二天去上课的路上，我才看到那条「深夜消息」。

examples.en: The organiser said a late-night message didn't require an immediate reply from anyone.
examples.zh: 组织者说，收到「深夜消息」谁都不用马上回复。

collocations: send a late-night message
read a late-night message
wait to answer a late-night message

words.enDefinition: a phrase reassuring someone that they can answer another time

examples.en: “No need to reply tonight,” I added because my classmate had an early shift.
examples.zh: 同学第二天早班，我就补了一句「今晚不用回复」。

examples.en: The organiser wrote, “No need to reply tonight,” under the message about rehearsals.
examples.zh: 组织者在排练消息下面写着「今晚不用回复」。

collocations: say “No need to reply tonight”
“No need to reply tonight if you're busy”
“No need to reply tonight if you're tired”

words.enDefinition: to share a message in the group area meant for its topic

examples.en: Our club moderator reminded us to post in the right channel for announcements.
examples.zh: 社团管理员提醒大家，要把公告「发到对应的频道」。

examples.en: I checked the topic list so I could post in the right channel.
examples.zh: 我查了话题列表，好「发到对应的频道」。

collocations: remember to post in the right channel
ask members to post in the right channel
post in the right channel for your topic

words.enDefinition: to mention all group members so they may receive a notification

examples.en: We agreed to tag everyone only when the rehearsal time changed suddenly.
examples.zh: 我们约好，只有排练时间突然变动时才「@群内所有人」。

examples.en: I chose not to tag everyone when sharing a link to a café.
examples.zh: 我分享咖啡馆链接时，决定不「@群内所有人」。

collocations: avoid having to tag everyone
choose whether to tag everyone
tag everyone in the group

words.enDefinition: to avoid passing the discussion or information beyond a group

examples.en: I asked people to keep this in the group until the schedule was final.
examples.zh: 我请大家在日程确定前「先别把这件事传出群」。

examples.en: The club coordinator wrote, “Please keep this in the group for now.”
examples.zh: 社团协调员写道「请暂时只在群里说这件事」。

collocations: please keep this in the group
ask people to keep this in the group
keep this in the group for now

words.zhGloss: 打电话前先问方不方便
words.enDefinition: to check that someone is ready to take a call before calling
acceptedZhAnswers: 打电话前先问方不方便

examples.en: My study partner asked me to ask before calling during her lab shift.
examples.zh: 学习伙伴请我在她实验室值班时「打电话前先问方不方便」。

examples.en: We agreed to ask before calling anyone in the group late at night.
examples.zh: 我们约好，深夜要给群里的人打电话时「先问方不方便」。

collocations: remember to ask before calling
agree to ask before calling
ask before calling late at night

words.zhGloss: 断章取义地引用别人的话
words.enDefinition: to repeat words without the surrounding information needed to understand them
acceptedZhAnswers: 断章取义地引用别人的话

examples.en: I did not want to quote someone out of context in our club newsletter.
examples.zh: 我不想在社团简报里「断章取义地引用别人的话」。

examples.en: Our editor explained how easy it was to quote someone out of context online.
examples.zh: 编辑解释了在网上多么容易「断章取义地引用别人的话」。

collocations: try not to quote someone out of context
be careful not to quote someone out of context
quote someone out of context in a post
